defects.description: Mirrored fist. She lies supine with her head at image-left, so her right side faces the camera and the raised arm (coming from the near shoulder, armpit visible) is her RIGHT arm. The fist shows its thumb side to the camera (thumb along the bottom with its nail visible, curled index forming the 'hole') while the back of the hand/knuckle ridge faces up. For a right hand with the back up and knuckles pointing away from the elbow, the thumb must face AWAY from the camera (toward her midline). Thumb-toward-camera + back-of-hand-up is left-hand geometry.

Forearm over-long: elbow to wrist crease is ~1000 px while her own fist measures ~250 px from wrist crease to knuckle (ratio ~4.0; a natural forearm is ~2.6x that length). The practitioner's nails at the elbow and wrist ends are about the same size, so perspective does not explain it; the forearm reads ~50% too long and ~1.8x her upper arm.
The practitioner's shirt, buttons, belt and trousers fill the top half and centre of the frame; the brief asks for an intimate close-up where only the two pairs of hands and forearms fill the frame.

Forearm is diagonal (~30 deg), not held level. The practitioner's hand now drapes the whole palm over the distal forearm just proximal to the wrist, fingers curled over the near side - better than the old fingertip claw but still not a flat palm resting on the back of the wrist.

Overlay is radius/ulna + forearm muscles with the red glow on the mid-forearm muscle belly (good) and no hand bones (the old metacarpal/carpal miscount is gone), but the proximal end also draws the distal humerus/elbow condyles.

notes: Hand-skeleton miscount no longer applies (no hand bones drawn) and the grip is improved, but the framing complaint (practitioner torso/belt in frame) is unchanged and two new body defects appeared (mirrored fist, over-long forearm). Practitioner face out of frame (top edge = shirt). Patient face visible (allowed). Background device screen blurred, no readable text. Overlay sits inside the forearm, oriented along it.
